0.why: Front view over the fence: ears spread either side, both eyes, the long face down to the muzzle at the bottom edge.

4.why: Still facing us; the head has drifted a little right with the camera. Holding the front view.

6.why: Still facing us, the muzzle just starting to slide right: the first small step of the turn.

8.why: The turn is under way: the face narrows on its right side and the far eye moves toward the right edge.

10.why: Turning: the muzzle swings right, the far eye is near the right edge and smaller.

12.why: Half turned, three-quarter view: the far eye sits at the edge of the face, the muzzle points down-right.

14.why: Past three-quarter: the far eye is a small mark on the edge of the face, about to go behind it.

16.why: Almost in profile, the far eye gone behind the face; the head starts to reach forward and down.

19.why: Full profile at the forward extreme: the head stretches out over the rail, muzzle furthest right.

20.why: Holding the forward reach for a moment before the head drops.

24.why: The head starts to tip down and, as it drops, begins to turn back toward us.

28.why: Head tipping down past the rails toward the hay, turning back toward the camera: the far eye comes out at the edge of the face.

30.why: Breakdown: the head hangs nearly straight down, half turned back toward us.

32.why: THE LINE: the muzzle reaches the hay; the head hangs from the poll, turned back toward us so both eyes show.

34.why: Settle after the contact: the muzzle pushes into the pile, the face nearly front-on.

36.why: Muzzle down in the hay pile, the head almost facing us, ears forward.

38.why: Eating: the muzzle in the pile, the lowest point of the bite.

40.why: Eating: the head lifts a little with a mouthful.

42.why: Eating: the muzzle drops back into the hay a little to the right.

44.why: Settle: nose in the hay, head down and facing us, chewing.
